title: fix: evaluate XPath against the document the server sent

raw.title: fix: evaluate XPath against the document the server sent
raw.body:
fix: evaluate XPath against the document the server sent

The XPath surface stripped namespaces with two regexes applied to the
whole serialized body before parsing, which also rewrote element text,
CDATA sections, and comments that merely contained namespace-shaped
characters, only recognized double-quoted xmlns declarations, and cost
two full-document allocations per evaluation.

The prepass is deleted. uppsala resolves namespaces natively and its
unprefixed XPath name tests match on local names, so //Body finds
soap:Body with no preprocessing, exactly as payload replacements
already relied on. Two deliberate behavior changes, both pinned by
tests: a document using an undeclared prefix is reported as invalid
XML instead of being silently rewritten into something parseable, and
a prefixed expression such as //f:x now matches when the document
declares the prefix.

Independently reviewed (fresh-context); review follow-ups included:
README and compliance-plan prose describing the old stripping
corrected, the bench case that reimplemented the deleted regexes now
measures the real parse-as-sent path, and the single-quoted test row
carries the prefixed assertion that actually discriminates old from
new. Closes finding F2 in the 2026-08-22 rust-code-smell audit.
